details: General linear form: ax + by + c = 0.
Solution is an ordered pair (u, v) satisfying the equation.
Every linear equation has infinitely many solutions forming a straight line graph.
evidence_or_examples: Fruit purchase equation 2x + 3y = 12 with intercepts (6, 0) and (0, 4).

details: Slope m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) measures steepness (rise over run).
Horizontal lines y = k have slope m = 0; vertical lines x = k have undefined slope.
Perpendicular lines satisfy m1 * m2 = -1; parallel lines satisfy m1 = m2.
Perpendicular distance from (x0, y0) to ax + by + c = 0: d = |ax0 + by0 + c| / sqrt(a^2 + b^2).
evidence_or_examples: Cycling uphill vs downhill physical intuition for positive/negative slope.
Distance from origin (0,0) to 3x + 4y - 10 = 0 is |-10| / 5 = 2.0 units.

details: No solution (parallel lines): a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2.
Infinitely many solutions (coincident lines): a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2.
evidence_or_examples: Solving 2x + 3y = 9 and 3x + 4y = 13 via elimination yields unique solution (3, 1).
Taxi fare modeling: fixed charge x plus rate y per km (x + 10y = 105, x + 15y = 155 => y = Rs 10/km, x = Rs 5).
